intentions.title: One content model, many document types: schemas, fields, and Expectation layouts define every document type generically instead of hardcoding tables per type
intentions.evidence: schema_definition.ex Ecto schema (fields, layout, prefill, initial_values, cross_validations, list_preview, owner_scoped) backs every doc type; writer.ex scaffold_expectation/apply_initial_values/maybe_apply_paper_template derive new documents from schema-declared layout+prefill+initial_values with dynamic tokens ($today); validation.ex + cross_validator.ex validate content against the same schema.

intentions.title: Hard multi-tenant isolation: every content read/write is scoped to workspace/project/owner and fails closed on missing scope, never fails open
intentions.evidence: scope.ex: scope_to_workspace(nil,_) -> where(false) (barkpark-s6t1), scope_to_owner(nil caller) -> owner_id IS NULL only (LOW-12), scope_to_grants fails closed to zero rows; writer.ex scopes prev_doc lookup to workspace/project before UPDATE (B3 mutate leak fix); graph.ex hydrate_nodes/fetch_doc/docs_by_id all pipe through scope_query so cross-tenant UUIDs hydrate to nothing.

intentions.title: Per-field visibility and encryption are enforced at a single output/write chokepoint so private, owner_only, and encrypted fields can never leak regardless of which surface reads them
intentions.evidence: envelope.ex render/3 is documented as the SINGLE redaction chokepoint (REST query, search, share-link, history, reference expansion all thread through it); nil caller fails closed to anonymous/public-only (fixes WS-B leak); field_readable?/2 also blocks filter/order side-channel probing of hidden fields; encryption.ex is the single write-side chokepoint (Writer.maybe_encrypt_marked_fields, fail-closed HIGH-3) pairing with envelope.ex's ciphertext-always-private read rule.

intentions.title: Give every document a navigable, bounded content graph (backlinks, orphans, broken references, force-sim graph pane) without ever leaking cross-tenant or unauthorized nodes
intentions.evidence: graph.ex traverse/2 BFS with node_budget 1000 / fan_out 200 / depth clamp 1..5, phantom/dangling node detection, rank_dependents ranks by topology never by weight (weight is layout-only), reverse_referencers/2 powers the Studio unpublish guard, all hydration paths apply Scope.scope_to_workspace_or_global + scope_to_owner so hidden nodes can't leak via the edge list either (MEDIUM-5 edge-half filter).

intentions.title: Optimistic-concurrency-safe, auditable writes: every mutation is rev-fenced against lost updates, deduped against duplicate task creation, and fanned out through a deferred (transaction-safe) broadcast/webhook/revision pipeline
intentions.evidence: writer.ex fenced_update/3 does a WHERE rev=expected UPDATE mirroring lifecycle's fenced_delete (ifmatch-unfenced-update); Tasks.Dedup.check_new_task gates duplicate task creation before insert; broadcast.ex documents the process-dict deferred-broadcast protocol (flush on commit, clear on rollback) that other content concerns rely on; mutation_event.ex + revision.ex persist an audit trail of every change.

intentions.title: Papers/Bulldocs and Sheets get a first-class content-graph-and-editor identity (block-based projection, sheet write-through) without becoming special-cased forks of the generic document write path
intentions.evidence: writer.ex maybe_apply_paper_template/ensure_block_ids/maybe_project_document_content give paper and block-bearing documents the same birth guarantee (pdd-t16) and project-on-write contract as the dedicated paper upsert path; sheets.ex hooks (maybe_recompute_sheet_formulas, hydrate_sheet_embed_snapshots, tap_sheet_writethrough) keep sheet embeds and their source sheet in sync through the same create/upsert chokepoint.

intentions.title: id/rev generation and legacy-envelope coercion keep the write API forgiving of both the flat Sanity-style envelope and the legacy content-map shape without ever losing a caller-supplied id
intentions.evidence: writer.ex from_envelope/1 preserves a Sanity-style `_id` when doc_id is absent (fixed a silent-drop bug); generate_id/1 draws 64 bits of entropy specifically to avoid the old collision-driven silent-overwrite bug (doc-id-collision-overwrite); draft_id.ex enforces the drafts.<id> prefix invariant on every create/upsert.
